topic.name: VCAP-VCF Prep
topic.title: Advanced VMware Cloud Foundation 9 Administrator (VCAP-VCF) Prep
topic.blurb: Unofficial study companion for the Advanced VMware Cloud Foundation 9 Administrator exam (3V0-11.26), leading to VMware Certified Advanced Professional - VMware Cloud Foundation Administrator. Every testable objective sits in Section 4 (Deploy, Configure, and Operate); Sections 1, 2, 3 and 5 carry no testable objectives in the current guide. Built from Broadcom's official exam guide (November 2026) and VCF 9 documentation areas. The vSphere Administration material also draws on the classic vSphere Virtual Machine Administration guide (ESXi 5.5, French edition), translated and rewritten for the durable VM fundamentals under objective 4.11; that book predates VCF, so treat it as grounding for VM concepts only, never for VCF 9 behavior.

tracks.label: VCAP-VCF Administrator (3V0-11.26)
tracks.summary: Advanced VMware Cloud Foundation 9 Administrator: 60 items in a 135-minute proctored Pearson VUE appointment, scaled passing score 300, USD 250. Item types include multiple-choice, multiple-selection, build-list, matching, drag-and-drop, point-and-click and hot-area. The minimally qualified candidate manages, maintains and scales a multi-region and/or multi-organization VCF private cloud across vCenter, ESX, vSAN, NSX, VCF Identity Broker, VCF Automation, VCF Operations (Logs, Fleet Management, Networks) and the vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS).

domains.name: vSAN and Storage
domains.description: Objectives 4.1-4.9: deploy vSAN and stretched clusters in a workload domain, supported non-vSAN storage, cross-cluster capacity sharing and vSAN storage clusters, vSAN encryption and data protection, Day 2 administration, storage policies.

domains.name: vSphere Administration
domains.description: Objectives 4.10-4.18: vSphere advanced settings, managing virtual machines, advanced network operations, CPU and memory performance optimization, vCenter performance, monitoring, security and access control, VM encryption and trusted environments.

domains.name: Provider Management
domains.description: Objectives 4.19-4.23: identity provider, provider content libraries, access control, blueprints and the Provider Consumption Organization in the VCF Automation Provider Management portal.

domains.name: VCF All Apps Tenancy
domains.description: Objectives 4.24-4.29: identity providers, access control, projects, governance policies, namespace classes, VPCs and VPC connectivity profiles inside a VCF All Apps organization.

domains.name: Supervisor and VKS
domains.description: Objectives 4.30-4.34: Supervisor clusters (NSX VPC, NSX segment, vDS, Avi load balancer), add-on services, VKS cluster updates, package repositories and registries, Supervisor upgrades.

domains.name: VCF Operations
domains.description: Objectives 4.35-4.43: Day 2 operational tasks, resource reclamation, rightsizing, capacity forecasting with what-if scenarios, cost management, policies, business vs operational intent, business applications, alerts.

domains.name: Fleet Management
domains.description: Objectives 4.44-4.47: scaling fleet lifecycle management, upgrading fleet components, VCF SSO with identity and access management, configuration drift monitoring in VCF Operations.

domains.name: VMware NSX
domains.description: Objectives 4.48-4.60: NSX Federation, NSX components, Edge clusters, Tier-0 gateways, VRFs, logical segments, Tier-1 gateways, VPCs, DHCP, NAT, projects and tenancy, advanced integrations, operational tasks (syslog, backup and restore).

exam.disclaimer: The real exam is scored on a scaled method (pass mark 300); Broadcom publishes no percentage equivalent, so this app's readiness scores are a study proxy, not a score prediction. The real exam also uses build-list, matching, drag-and-drop, point-and-click and hot-area items that a multiple-choice app cannot reproduce; use the drills for process-order thinking. All 60 testable objectives are in Section 4; Sections 1, 2, 3 and 5 have no testable objectives in the November 2026 guide.

roadmap.title: Your path to VCAP-VCF Administrator
roadmap.intro: One exam: Advanced VMware Cloud Foundation 9 Administrator (3V0-11.26), 60 items, 135 minutes, scaled pass 300, USD 250 at Pearson VUE. There is no stated prerequisite, but the exam assumes you already run VCF: it is all Section 4, deploy, configure and operate, weighted toward NSX (13 objectives), vSAN, vSphere administration and VCF Operations (9 each).
roadmap.footer: Official pages: certification page · exam study guide · VCF 9.0 Tech Docs.
